newsitem.title: USA: Diba names ex-Zenith CEO as vice chairman.
newsitem.headline: Diba names ex-Zenith CEO as vice chairman.

text.p: Internet start-up Diba Inc. said Thursday it named former Zenith Electronics Corp. Chief Executive Albin Moschner to the new full-time post of vice chairman and also to its board of directors.
The Menlo Park, Calif.-based company also named Pacific Telesis Group Chief Executive Michael Fitzpatrick to the board.

Closely held Diba is a Silicon Valley company that has developed software that allows devices such as telephones and televisions to be hooked up to the Internet, creating a new category of so-called "information appliances."

Unlike current personal computers, which many consumers find complex to purchase, use and maintain, Diba-based information appliances are intended to enable average consumers to be able to afford to tap into the information age for the first time.
As vice chairman of Diba, Moschner, working from a new office in Chicago, will be responsible for establishing strategic partnerships with consumer electronics companies, Diba said.

In May, Glenview, Ill.-based Zenith said it would incorporate the Diba technology into its NetVision Internet TVs, allowing users to browse the World Wide Web and read electronic mail in the comfort of their living rooms.
The announcement of plans to develop an Internet TV helped spark a wild run-up in Zenith's stock price to above $25 from around $6 previously. The stock slipped 87.5 cents to $16 Thursday.
Japan's NEC Corp. has also agreed to a deal with Diba to create a new semiconductor chip and software combination for use in such information appliances.
Samsung Electronics Co. Ltd. has said it plans to create a new line of Internet-enabled televisions based on Diba software.
The company was founded by two brothers, Farzad Dibachi, former head of Oracle Corp.'s New Media unit, and Farid Dibachi, who worked for several years at Hewlett-Packard Co.
Diba is contemplating an initial public offering, perhaps as early as this fall, Red Herring magazine reported in its August issue. The company declined to comment on the report.
